messages:
Noelle T.: quick alert  several SAST runs started failing with "ownership unresolved" and a few DAST jobs erroring with KMS:PermissionDenied after the config push early this morning.

Noelle T.: snippet: ```
2025-10-11T07:02:12Z sast: owner-resolver: git blame: 403 Forbidden
2025-10-11T07:02:13Z dast: unwrap secret: KMS PermissionDenied key projects/redwood-inference/locations/global/keyRings/ci/cryptoKeys/artifact-key
```

Omar V.: cc @infra-terraform @sec-oncall  which change was applied? I saw a terraform plan that consolidated a few bindings.

infra-terraform: we merged PR 5234 to reduce group:ci-broad-write. The plan removed an explicit roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter binding from serviceAccount:scanner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com and replaced it with group membership we thought included the scanner. Likely drift or group removal caused the effective loss.

Yara H.: fwiw the ownership service does two things: repo read for CODEOWNERS+blame and audit lookup for historical ownership. If either fails we can return ownerless. The audit exporter also showed a tiny gap around 07:01-07:04UTC.

sec-oncall: collect the request IDs and exact window. If audit logs are missing we should export what we have and open cloud support. Also confirm whether scanner uses wrapped/ephemeral keys that require explicit stable grants across rotations.

Noelle T.: request ids: s-rq-71a / s-rq-71b. Gap: 2025-10-11T07:01:58Z - 2025-10-11T07:04:22Z. Exporting logs now to gs://sec-exports/1788202020/partial/

CI-bot: pipeline: manual-retrigger queued for affected PRs.

Omar V.: immediate fix: readd explicit decrypt binding to the scanner SA and add roles/source.reader so ownership resolver can read repo metadata until we sort group memberships. Command I ran: 
```bash
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-inference
  --member=serviceAccount:scanner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter

gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-inference
  --member=serviceAccount:scanner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  --role=roles/source.reader
```

infra-terraform: added the same bindings to terraform modules and bumped the retention on the sink resource to prevent accidental removal. Pushing a plan to lock this in.

Yara H.: after re-adding grants, I cleared owner-service cache for the monorepo and requeued checks. Some SAST jobs cleared, but ~8 PRs still show ownerless due to resolver timeouts returning 502 during the incident window.

Noelle T.: Proposal (short-term): change pipeline to treat ownership-resolver 5xx/timeout as non-blocking and fall back to parsing in-repo CODEOWNERS (label OWNER:inferred). Will open PR with feature-flag owner.fallback=true.

product-security: please tag payment/billing teams  their PRs might be in the backlog.

Noelle T.: pinged @product-security @payments. Also filing tickets: SEC-5691 rehydrate-scanner-iam, SEC-5692 owner-fallback-feature, SEC-5693 audit-log-cloud-support. Assigning infra + sec-oncall.

sec-oncall: add the cloud support case with exported bucket path and request ids s-rq-71a/s-rq-71b. If they can't reconstruct the gap, ask for SLA exception or extended retention for adjacent windows. Also add a pre-apply checklist item: list all SAs used by CI and ensure explicit bindings survive refactors.

Omar V.: agreed. Follow-ups for infra: 1) infra module change to include a 'consumers' map for service accounts 2) add unit test in ci-infra that simulates KMS rotation + binding changes 3) update RBAC playbook to include quick rollback steps.

Yara H.: will land the owner-fallback PR behind a flag and emit a metric when fallback is used so we can monitor regressions. Also will document the audit-gap timeline in the postmortem draft.

Noelle T.: thanks everyone. I'll update SEC tickets with logs & commands and post the postmortem draft in #incidents when ready. Keep this channel as the canonical incident thread. :thumbsup:
